title: Collect employee names into a `Set<String>` (removing duplicates).
shortTitle: Collect employee names into a Set<String> (removing duplicates)
keyPoints: map(Employee::getName).collect(toSet()) gathers names into a Set, automatically removing duplicates
A Set stores each element once by equals and hashCode, so no explicit distinct() is needed
toSet() returns a HashSet by default with no guaranteed iteration order
For sorted order use toCollection(TreeSet::new); for insertion order use toCollection(LinkedHashSet::new)
Deduplication relies on correct equals and hashCode on the element type (String has them)
toSet() is equivalent to distinct().collect(toList()) but expresses the uniqueness intent directly

s1_definition.oneliner: `map(getName).collect(toSet())` collects distinct names into a `Set`, dropping duplicates automatically because a set stores each value only once.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **map(Employee::getName)** extracts the name from each employee.
- **collect(Collectors.toSet())** gathers names into a `Set<String>` that holds each value once.
- **Deduplication** is automatic: the set uses `equals` and `hashCode` to detect duplicates.
- **No guaranteed order**: `toSet()` returns a `HashSet` by default.
- **For ordered sets**, use `toCollection(TreeSet::new)` or `toCollection(LinkedHashSet::new)`.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, Priya compiles a mailing list of unique employee names. If two employees share the same name, it appears only once in the list.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Input: [Rajesh, Priya, Rajesh, Meera, Priya]
       │
       │  collect(toSet())
       ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │  HashSet<String>             │
  │  {Rajesh, Priya, Meera}     │
  │  ← duplicates removed       │
  │  ← order not guaranteed     │
  └──────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Collecting names into a `Set` with `map(getName).collect(toSet())` automatically removes duplicates because a set holds each element only once by `equals` and `hashCode`. No explicit `distinct()` call is needed. At the National Bank of India, Priya uses this for mailing lists where each name should appear once.

The default `toSet()` returns a `HashSet` with no guaranteed iteration order. For sorted order, use `toCollection(TreeSet::new)`. For insertion order (first-seen order), use `toCollection(LinkedHashSet::new)`. The choice depends on whether the consumer needs ordering.

For custom objects, deduplication is only as good as their `equals` and `hashCode`. If those are not implemented correctly, the set will not dedupe as expected. Records are safe because they auto-generate correct `equals` and `hashCode` from all components.

Remember one sentence: `toSet()` collects distinct values automatically because a set holds each element once, but use `toCollection` with a supplier when ordering matters.
